newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU taxes wheat exports to protect domestic supply.
newsitem.headline: EU taxes wheat exports to protect domestic supply.

text.p: The European Union on Thursday slapped a tax on daily exports of soft wheat to safeguard supplies for domestic consumers at affordable prices, a European Commission spokesman said.
The move follows a prolonged dry spell in Europe. It sent Chicago wheat futures racing higher.
The spokesman confirmed that the EU set daily export taxes of 15 Ecus a tonne on soft wheat, 20 Ecus on wheat flour, 10 Ecus on durum wheat and 15 Ecus on durum wheat semolina.
"With market uncertainty about future supplies, we believe it is prudent to curb exports to ensure adequate supplies at reasonable prices," Commission agriculture spokesman Gerard Kiely said.
Kiely said the tax was imposed because the market was over-heating due to internal and external climatic influences.
He was referring to frost damage to crops in the U.S. and a prolonged spell of dry weather in much of the European Union.

"The cereals industry tends to see the CAP (Common Agricultural Policy) as a means of preventing prices falling too low but the Commission has an equal responsibility to stop prices going too high," Kiely added.
Soft wheat prices have soared above EU intervention levels by 25.5 percent in Italy, 20 percent in Britain, 15 percent in France and by 9.5 percent in Germany.
The EU last week prematurely closed 1996/97 (July/June) weekly wheat export tenders in a bid to dampen domestic prices.
The EU imposed a wheat export tax in October 1995 in order to conserve dwindling stocks and stop prices spiralling through the roof.
